Definition: a contraction from G4731 (as stiff and unnatural); "sterile":--barren.
BiblicalUsage: Barren is the word for the womb that bears no child, and for the promise that breaks the barrenness. Elisabeth was barren and well stricken in years, yet she conceived a son in her old age, and Paul quotes Isaiah, Rejoice, thou barren that bearest not, for the desolate hath many more children than she which hath an husband.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the barren woman is the Bible's picture of hopelessness turned to joy, and the desolate ends up with more children than the fruitful.
